Confirm goal

Harden SVG generation in bench/report.py against text injection while keeping the CLI, the Markdown tables and the published datasets unchanged.  Current state - Three SVG writers, all in bench/report.py: chart() (:88), hero() (:146) and long_hero() (:218, via hero); the plugins chart (:~560) goes through chart(). - Dynamic text reaches markup at: the aria-label attribute in chart() and hero(); <text> nodes for title, subtitle, panel name, LABELS.get(b, b) build labels, fmt() values, ratio_text()/compared() notes; plugin column names built from dataset build ids (names = f"{LABELS.get(k[0], k[0])}, ..."); step_name() built from pauses.jsonl step keys. - No escaping exists today. Confirmed: `--label 'bun=Bun & <script>alert(1)</script>'` produces bench-speed-light.svg that xml.etree.ElementTree rejects ("not well-formed (invalid token)", line 10). Label text also flows into Markdown table headers (header = ["", *[LABELS.get(x, x) ...]]), so escaping at that boundary would corrupt the docs tables. - Output is deterministic (same folder + args twice -> byte-identical SVGs), so a before/after diff is a usable gate. No other Python SVG producer exists; CI runs only `python3 -m py_compile bench/*.py` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:102).  Decisions (conservative, standard library only; stated where the seed was ambiguous) 1. Escaping is applied at each SVG insertion point inside chart()/hero(), not at the data boundary. Rationale: LABELS and plugin names are shared with the Markdown tables, so boundary escaping would print `&` in docs and double-escape anything reused in two formats. Alternative rejected: an element/attribute builder rewriting all writers (unrelated refactoring). 2. Mechanism: xml.sax.saxutils.escape for element text and xml.sax.saxutils.quoteattr for attribute values (it selects the quote character itself), both wrapped in two tiny local helpers so a single place owns the policy.
